g.text: 1.User should be able to view events
2.user shpuld be able to search for a event
3.User should be able to book tickt for a event
1. System should be highly consistent for booking ticekt
and in all other case system should be highly available
2. System should be scalable and high throughput for popluar events
3. system should be low latency on search (<500ms)
4.system is read heavy and should handle high throughput on read (100:1)
1. USER : stores user information like name , contact etc..
2. EVENT : stores event detail like date , type , desc , performer etc....
3. PERFORMER : stores performer detail invloved in an event
4. VENUE : stroes venue detail where the event is going to happen
5. TICKET : stores info about ticket for an event , seats details, pricing and status of availability
5. BOOKING : stores booking detail like totoal price , ticked booked , user ...
why useing this inplace of inverted index (GS)
- it requries search on different values of feild not just onces
and elastic search is effienct doing this
- use change data capture (CDC) for real-time or near-real-time data synchronization from PostgreSQL to Elasticsearch
WHy postgres ? - we need ACID transactions for booking so opting postgres
